Title: Mitra Tamil empowerment programme: RM900k allocation benefits 8,690 SPM, STPM students
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 8,690 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) and Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM) candidates nationwide have benefited from the 2026 Tamil Language Excellence Empowerment Programme, involving an allocation of RM901,680.
The Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (Mitra), under the Human Resources Ministry (Kesuma), said the programme was implemented in collaboration with the Education Ministry (MOE) to improve academic performance and Tamil language proficiency.
The initiative was part of the government's efforts to support students from the Indian community through focused academic preparation, while boosting their motivation, self-confidence and examination readiness, it said in a statement today.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said 7,897 SPM candidates and 793 STPM candidates who sat for the Tamil Language paper nationwide had benefited from the programme.
"We want to ensure every student has the opportunity to achieve excellence, regardless of their background. Through Mitra, we are not merely providing educational assistance, but implementing academic interventions that can directly impact student achievement.
"Tamil language is not merely a subject to be mastered for examinations, but a treasure trove of language, culture and identity that must be preserved by future generations," he said.
Ramanan earlier officiated the programme at the Omnia Auditorium, Menara BAC, Petaling Jaya, which was attended by nearly 300 SPM candidates and 50 educators from Selangor.
Mitra said it would continue to expand educational initiatives under Kalvi Madani, including through strategic collaborations with MOE, state education departments and relevant institutions, to extend access to targeted academic development programmes for more students from the Indian community.

Title: KTMB records 7 railway trespassing cases in nine months
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) recorded seven cases of people trespassing on railway tracks between January and September this year, disrupting train services.
In the latest incident, an SUV entered the tracks at Port Klang Station on Sunday, causing delays to train services.
KTMB said the vehicle entered the tracks through a level crossing gate. The driver was not injured. The vehicle was removed and the tracks cleared.
An inspection found no damage to the railway tracks, signalling systems or overhead line equipment, it said.
A video showing the
SUV on the tracks
went viral on social media.
KTMB warned that trespassing, vandalism and cable theft could disrupt train services and endanger passengers and railway personnel.
Damaging railway property are serious offences under the Railways Act 1991 and the Land Public Transport Act 2010, which provide for penalties including fines, imprisonment or both upon conviction, it said in a statement.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Yeo proposes Langkawi or Penang as Disney cruise hub
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia should negotiate with Disney Cruise Line to make Langkawi or Penang a departure and arrival hub for its Disney Adventure cruise ship, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Yeo Bee Yin (PH-Puchong) said Malaysia should aim to become more than just a port of call by allowing international tourists to begin or end their cruises at either destination.
"I don't think we should be content with merely being a port of call.
"I propose that the Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry begin strategic negotiations with Disney Cruise Line to explore the possibility of making Langkawi or Penang an official embarkation and disembarkation port," she said when debating the 2027 Budget.
Yeo said the arrangement could encourage tourists to spend several days in Malaysia before or after their cruise, benefiting the local tourism industry.
"Imagine the economic spillover. Tourists who begin or end their cruises in Langkawi could spend several days there before or after their voyage," she said.
She said Disney Adventure, which operates out of Singapore, was scheduled to make its first stop in Langkawi during a four-night cruise departing Singapore on Dec 31.
Yeo estimated that the ship, which can accommodate between 6,000 and 6,700 passengers, could make 25 to 30 visits a year, potentially bringing 150,000 to 200,000 passenger movements to Langkawi.
She said spending of between RM250 and RM400 per passenger could generate an estimated RM35 million to RM80 million in direct annual spending on the island, benefiting local businesses.
"However, the main question is whether these tourists will come ashore and spend money, or simply remain on board," she said.
Yeo said lengthy immigration queues and severe traffic congestion could discourage cruise passengers from disembarking, adding that immigration authorities had a crucial role in ensuring smooth arrivals.
She also called for upgrades to international airports to accommodate growing tourist demand and urged the ministry to pursue the proposed arrangement with Disney Cruise Line.

Title: United Malacca's executive director Lip Sin passes away
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: United Malacca Bhd has announced that its executive director Datuk Seri Tee Lip Sin has passed away at the age of 55.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the plantation company said Tee began his career as an executive at Prosper Capital Holdings Sdn Bhd in 1995 before rising to become an executive director.
He was the group managing director of Prosper Group and a director of Prosper Capital Holdings, a substantial shareholder of United Malacca.
Tee also served as a director of Australia-listed PRL Global Ltd, Phosphate Resources (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd, Phosphate Resources (Singapore) Pte Ltd and several private companies involved in plantation and milling businesses.
He held a Master of Business Administration from the University of Sunderland and a degree in Business Administration from the University of Wales.
Tee held 1.98 million United Malacca shares directly and 179,700 shares indirectly, through his spouse and children.
His death came two days after United Malacca announced a mandatory general offer (MGO) at RM6.10 a share by Prosper Trading Sdn Bhd, Tee Kim Tee and Tee Cheng Hua.
The offer followed Prosper Trading's acquisition of a 13.44 per cent stake in United Malacca from Great Eastern Life Assurance (Malaysia) Bhd for RM171.93 million.
United Malacca shares were halted an hour after the announcement before closing unchanged at RM6.04, valuing the company at RM1.27 billion.

Title: IMF chief urges urgent fiscal action as global economic resilience reaches limits
Article:
ISTANBUL: IMF managing director Kristalina Georgieva on Wednesday urged governments to urgently strengthen public finances, warning that the global economy's resilience to repeated shocks is reaching its limits, Anadolu Ajansi reported.
Speaking at a press briefing during the IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, Georgieva said energy and fiscal buffers were being depleted, while persistent inflation and rising interest rates were adding to debt-servicing pressures.
Global growth is projected at about 3.1 per cent in 2026, unchanged from April's forecast but below last year's 3.4 per cent, she said.
The outlook reflects opposing forces, with the war in West Asia disrupting energy supplies while demand linked to artificial intelligence supports economic activity.
Economies integrated into AI supply chains, including Thailand, Malaysia, South Korea and Singapore, were generally performing better, along with energy exporters unaffected by wars.
Low-income countries and fragile states, particularly energy importers excluded from the technology boom, faced the greatest pressures.
Georgieva said government bond yields in advanced economies had risen to multidecade highs, reflecting inflation, investment demand, expectations of stronger AI-driven growth and fiscal weaknesses.
Higher benchmark yields were increasing borrowing costs for emerging markets even where their risk premiums remained stable, she said, warning that elevated financing costs were likely to persist.
Debt-servicing costs in low-income countries had increased from 6 per cent of government revenues a decade ago to 14 per cent, she added.
Georgieva urged governments to raise revenues, rationalise spending and improve public financial management. Assistance to offset rising food and energy costs should be temporary and targeted at vulnerable people while preserving price signals.
Central banks should remain focused on price stability, with the strongest case for tightening in economies where inflation exceeds targets and activity remains robust.
On global imbalances, she called on China to boost domestic consumption, the US to increase savings and reduce deficits, and Europe to strengthen investment.
US economic growth alone would not deliver the required fiscal adjustment quickly enough, making additional measures necessary, she said.
Georgieva also warned that disappointing near-term AI returns could trigger a disorderly market correction, while AI-enabled cyberattacks posed risks to financial stability.

Title: Infomina's net profit rose 30.6pct in Q1
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Infomina Bhd's net profit rose 30.6 per cent to RM10.55 million in the first quarter ended Aug 31, 2026 (Q1 FY27), from RM8.08 million a year ago.
The increase was mainly due to higher profit contribution from the technology infrastructure operations, maintenance and support services segment, the group said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia.
Quarterly revenue rose 39.5 per cent to RM76.19 million from RM54.63 million previously, driven by higher revenue contribution from the same segment.
Earnings per share increased to 1.76 sen from 1.34 sen previously.
Infomina's outstanding order book stood at RM614.2 million following contracts secured in Malaysia from the Road Transport Department (JPJ) and a local financial institution, as well as a contract from Panasonic Digital Co Ltd in Japan.
The group also completed the acquisition of a 51 per cent stake in Blue Fortress Sdn Bhd, which is expected to strengthen its cybersecurity, digital transformation and managed technology services businesses.
Separately, Broadcom appointed Infomina to distribute and support its mainframe software portfolio in 12 Asia Pacific markets, including four new markets: Australia, New Zealand, South Korea and India.
The group already operates in Malaysia, Thailand, the Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan, Hong Kong, China and Japan.
Overall, the board remains optimistic about the group's outlook despite ongoing global economic uncertainties, barring unforeseen circumstances.
It said the recent developments, together with disciplined execution, were expected to support the group's growth.

Title: FBM KLCI expansion to better reflect Malaysia's economy, stock weighting impact manageable – AHAM Capital
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The expansion of the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) from 30 to 50 constituents is expected to provide a more accurate representation of Malaysia's domestic economy.
The impact on the weightings of existing constituents is expected to be manageable, according to AHAM Asset Management Bhd (AHAM Capital).
Its deputy head of equity (Malaysia), David Loh, said the expansion would provide broader coverage of the domestic market, which has long been represented by a relatively small number of companies, while allowing the performance of more sectors, particularly technology, to be reflected in the benchmark index.
"For the longest time, the biggest comment about the Malaysian index is that it is very much in the old economy sector. A lot of technology stocks have done well in the past, but their performance was not captured in the FBM KLCI because they were not in there.
"With these technology stocks coming in, that will help the new index going forward," he told Bernama on the sidelines of a media engagement and networking session with AHAM Capital fund managers here today.
The implementation will take place from Dec 21, 2026, with Phase 1 seeing 20 new constituents added to the FBM KLCI at 50 per cent of their final index weight.
In Phase 2, the 20 new constituents will reach 100 per cent of their final index weight, completing the transition to the enhanced FBM KLCI effective June 21, 2027.
Loh said the phased implementation was intended to minimise market disruption as the inclusion of 20 new constituents would dilute the weightings of the existing 30 constituents.
"Based on the early calculation by the index strategist, the impact on their weightings should not be more than a high single digit," he said.
He added that the transition was designed to minimise disruption and that the overall impact was expected to be manageable.
Following the expansion of the FBM KLCI, the FBM 70 will be reduced from 70 to 50 constituents and renamed the FTSE Bursa Malaysia Mid Cap Index.
The FTSE Bursa Malaysia Top 100 Index will remain unchanged at 100 constituents.

Title: Penang's RM114.8mil Sungai Pinang flood mitigation project 50.86pct complete
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang's RM114.8 million Sungai Pinang flood mitigation project is 50.86 per cent complete, with full completion scheduled for Sept 20, 2027.
State Infrastructure Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the project aimed to reduce flash flood risks across the 51sq km Sungai Pinang river basin, where rapid development had placed increasing pressure on existing drainage infrastructure.
"The project is expected to reduce the flood-affected area in parts of the Sungai Pinang basin by 10.15 per cent, while reducing damage to public infrastructure, residents' properties, housing and transport links," he said during a visit to Phase One of the Sungai Pinang river basin flood mitigation plan.
The project, which began on Sept 21, 2023, is designed to provide flood protection against events with a 100-year average recurrence interval.
Its scope includes deepening and widening a 1.4km stretch of Sungai Pinang, constructing 1.02km of parallel drains and upgrading drainage outfalls to improve stormwater flow towards the sea.
The works also include a piano weir and a pumping station equipped with four screw pumps, two on each riverbank, each with a capacity of 2.0 cubic metres per second.
An ancillary building is also being constructed.
The 3.2km Sungai Pinang serves as the main drainage channel for the river basin in Penang's northeast district, discharging water into the sea.
Rapid development in the surrounding catchment has altered land levels and surface water flows, while the existing drainage system has struggled to cope with higher water volumes, particularly during heavy rainfall, increasing the risk of flash floods.
Zairil said the state government remained committed to ensuring the project was implemented effectively and would continue to monitor its progress to ensure its
flood-reduction objectives
were achieved sustainably.
"The project is expected to help minimise flood-related losses and strengthen protection for communities and infrastructure in vulnerable parts of the basin," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tuanku Muhriz: Royal succession disputes must follow adat, law
Article:
KUALA PILAH: Disputes over royal succession in Negeri Sembilan must be resolved in accordance with adat or customary law and legal provisions, rather than personal interests.
Negri Sembilan Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir said the authority of the royal institution must be upheld through integrity, justice and responsibility, warning that actions contrary to established customs could undermine public confidence and threaten the state's stability.
He said said Adat Perpatih and the law formed the foundation of the position of the Ruler and succession to the throne in Negri Sembilan, while adat institutions, including the Undang Yang Empat, Lembaga, Ibu Soko, Buapak and Anak Buah, represented an important heritage passed down through generations to preserve traditions and maintain stability.
"Those who, over the past several months, have taken actions that sparked disputes over succession rules in the name of defending adat must understand that adat cannot be defended by violating its own rules.
"Such actions not only risk undermining the authority of customary institutions and the palace but could also destabilise the state and erode public trust," he said in his royal address at the installation ceremony of Datuk Azrin Khairi as the 17th Undang of Jelebu at Istana Besar Seri Menanti here.
The ceremony was also attended by Tunku Ampuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-'Abidin.
State Secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and heads of state government departments were in attendance.
Tuanku Muhriz said the authority of the institution of the Ruler depends on respect for adat, the supremacy of the Constitution and the rule of law.
"The high and noble position of the Ruler comes with a great trust and responsibility. The trust of the people, in turn, is an essential foundation for ensuring that this institution continues to be respected and preserved.
"As the Malay proverb says, Raja adil raja disembah, raja zalim raja disanggah (a just ruler is revered, a tyrannical ruler is opposed); justice and integrity must always be the foundation of leadership.
Tuanku Muhriz urged all parties to learn from history and not allow personal interests to override truth and justice at the expense of the state's security, well-being and longstanding heritage.
He said adat is not merely a heritage to take pride in, but a trust that must be preserved and defended with full responsibility.
"Indeed, the future and stability of Negeri Sembilan depend on the readiness of all of us to respect adat, to obey the law, and to place the interests of the state above personal interest, for the sake of generations to come," he said.
His Royal Highness concluded by expressing hope that Negeri Sembilan Darul Khusus continues to be at peace and prosperous, with its institution of monarchy, its adat heritage and the unity of its people always preserved.  — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Don't politicise Negri Sembilan crisis, say Malay rulers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malay Rulers have warned against outside interference and attempts to politicise the Negri Sembilan royal crisis, saying the dispute must be resolved through lawful channels by the relevant authorities.
In a statement issued today, the Malay Rulers said the issue must not be exploited for political gain, to garner public support or to expand influence in pursuit of power.
"Contradictory and irresponsible statements will only exacerbate the situation, heighten tensions, confuse the public and tarnish the dignity of the royal institution," the statement read.
The statement was issued by Keeper of the Rulers' Seal Tan Sri Syed Danial Syed Ahmad in accordance with the royal decree of the Malay Rulers.
It said statements or actions made without a proper understanding of the state's customs, history and constitutional framework could further aggravate the situation and undermine social harmony.
The public was also cautioned against spreading unverified information or being swayed by narratives that could divide society.
"The relevant authorities should be given the time and space to discharge their responsibilities and fulfil the trust placed in them with prudence, wisdom and sound judgement," the statement said.
The Malay Rulers called on all parties involved in the dispute to exercise wisdom and patience, and respect the proper conduct, customs and dignity of the royal institution.
They said differences in position should be resolved through lawful and duly authorised channels, in accordance with established customs and the provisions of the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959.
"Consultation should be pursued with the utmost sincerity to achieve a dignified resolution without belittling or insulting any party," the statement said.
The statement also stressed that the throne represented a sacred trust carrying great responsibility towards the state and its people.
It said the spirit of kinship, social harmony and respect for the royal institution must be upheld throughout efforts to resolve the dispute.
All parties were urged to refrain from making statements that could cause humiliation or taking actions that could worsen the situation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 5 men sought over Semenyih murder
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Police are hunting five men believed to be involved in the murder of a local man whose body was found buried in Semenyih, Kajang.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said 15 suspects, including two foreigners, had been arrested, with several already charged in court.
He said the investigation began after the victim's wife lodged a police report when she could not contact her husband for several hours.
The arrests involve three separate cases: kidnapping, murder and firearms-related offences.
The five men still at large are known as Dedek, Jimmy Boy, Amen, Yeye and Apak, he said at a press conference at the Selangor police contingent headquarters.
Shazeli said the suspects, aged between 35 and 48, were believed to be in Selangor.
Investigations also found that the suspects were involved in gangsterism, with almost all having committed various criminal and drug-related offences, he said.
The victim was believed to have been abducted by several suspects in a car from the Ampang Waterfront area between 4am and 4.30am on Sept 24.
Shazeli said police were taken to the location where the victim was murdered and buried in Semenyih on Sept 27.
The victim was believed to have been detained and tortured before being killed and buried. A post-mortem found that he died from multiple incised wounds to the neck.
Investigations found that the 42-year-old self-employed man was killed following a disagreement between him and the suspects, he said.
The discovery of the body led to several arrests. Police also seized two shotguns, a Proton Wira and a hoe believed to have been used to bury the victim.
Shazeli said several of the 15 suspects arrested were charged at the Ampang and Bangi courts.
Media reports said the victim, identified as Mulia and believed to be in his 30s, was taken away in a Honda.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'It takes a nation to raise a child': MP calls for joint action on school safety
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Concerns over nihilistic violent extremism (NVE) among schoolchildren require joint action by the government, schools and parents, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
NVE refers to an emerging form of extremism involving violence without a clear political, religious or conventional ideological agenda.
Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin (PN-Masjid Tanah) said the ideology was believed to have spread among pupils, raising concerns that they could be drawn into violence.
"This ideology is believed to have spread among pupils, and this is deeply worrying. It has become a frightening crisis," she said when debating the 2027 Budget.
She said education policies played a crucial role in shaping future generations, with their effects often becoming apparent only 15 to 20 years later.
"In the past, we could say, 'It takes a village to raise a child', but things have changed. Now, 'It takes a nation to raise a child'," she said.
Mas Ermieyati said teachers needed adequate support to identify pupils experiencing emotional distress, learning difficulties or food insecurity while managing their classes.
She also called on the government to publish regular reports on school safety audits, critical repair needs, teacher vacancies by specialisation and learning outcomes.
Parents, she said, should also reflect on their responsibilities rather than placing all the blame on schools, teachers and ministers when children were harmed.
"What about our attitudes as parents? When was the last time mothers and fathers checked their children's schoolbags before they went to school?" she asked.
She also questioned whether the Health Ministry received data from the Education Ministry on pupils' mental health and psychological wellbeing to support targeted interventions in schools.
"If the Health Ministry itself does not have that data, how can it carry out targeted and effective interventions?" she added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Oil prices surge as Iran deploys new tactics to target tankers
Article:
LONDON: Oil prices rose on Wednesday after an attack on the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil company, while Iranian officials told Reuters they were deploying new tactics to target ships, seeking to keep oil prices high and influence US midterm elections.
Brent crude futures rose 91 cents, or 0.9 per cent, to US$106.60 a barrel at 1110 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude rose US$1.65, or 1.8 per cent, to US$95.79 a barrel, its highest in more than two weeks.
"Attacks on ships crossing the Strait of Hormuz and military strikes between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis are supporting prices as market participants remain concerned about lower oil exports from the region," said UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo, adding that exports had held up so far.
Iranian officials declined to provide details of the new strategy to target ships, but one said Iran had started using different offensive tactics about 10 days ago.
"That Iranian officials are openly admitting to undermining US efforts to keep oil prices under control speaks volumes about the real intentions behind the so-called 'peace talks'," said Priyanka Sachdeva, head of market insights at Phillip Nova.
ATTACKS ON MULTIPLE FRONTS
The Iran-allied Houthis attacked an administrative building belonging to state-owned oil company Saudi Aramco in the city of Dhahran, causing a limited fire, Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said on Wednesday.
The group has fired ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia over the past week in retaliation for the kingdom's support of Yemeni government forces. Riyadh's international airport has been hit four times, with a strike on Saturday killing 13 people.
Meanwhile, a container ship sank in waters south of the Strait of Hormuz after hitting a naval mine and catching fire, Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said in a statement shared by state media on Wednesday. This came a day after the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said a container ship and a tanker had been hit by unknown projectiles within the strait.
"The expectation that increased Russian diesel exports will ease market tightness is likely to limit sharp price movement in either direction," said Hiroyuki Kikukawa, chief strategist at Nissan Securities Investment.
US President Donald Trump announced last Friday that Russia had agreed to supply diesel to global markets, and his administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel designed to deprive Moscow of revenue for its war in Ukraine.
Russia's crude oil production increased by 65,000 barrels per day in September to 8.43 million barrels per day but remained 870,000 barrels per day lower year-on-year, the International Energy Agency said on Wednesday.
The IEA also said that a lack of operational Russian refinery capacity meant the recently announced easing of Russian diesel export restrictions was unlikely to bring any material change to the global gasoil market balance.
Constrained diesel supplies could persist well into next year, the IEA also said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Couple jailed up to 8 years over man's death in Kelantan
Article:
KOTA BARU: The High Court here today sentenced a couple to seven and eight years in prison for causing a man's death by negligence in Kampung Gondang, Ketereh, four years ago.
Judge Datuk Azhar Mokhtar sentenced Maizatul Shima Abdullah, 25, to eight years' imprisonment, while Muhammad Za'im Syakir Sha'ari, 24, was jailed for seven years.
The sentences are to take effect from the dates of their respective arrests.
The couple were charged with jointly committing the offence at an old Muslim cemetery in Kampung Gondang between 10pm on May 14, 2022, and 1am the following day.
They were charged under Section 304(a) of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same code, in connection with the death of Muhamad Fahmi Adli Mat.
In delivering his decision, Azhar said the court had considered submissions by deputy public prosecutor Hazwanie Husain Bustari, including the seriousness of the offence.
The court also took into account the fact that the victim's body had been concealed and was only discovered several days later.
However, the judge considered mitigating factors, including the young age of both accused, before deciding on the sentences.
The court also ordered both accused to pay RM2,500 each in compensation to the victim's family under Section 425A of the Criminal Procedure Code.
Both will face an additional six months' imprisonment if they fail to pay the compensation.
The court registrar will determine the method of payment to the victim's family.
Maizatul was represented by lawyers Azahir Nasir and Nurul Amira Mohd Zaidi, while Za'im was represented by Datuk Ahmad Zaidi Zainal and Fatini Athirah Baharin.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit closes higher against US dollar on improved risk appetite
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed higher against the greenback on Wednesday as investors' risk appetite improved ahead of US inflation data, with sentiment supported by the 2027 Budget announcement last week.
At 6pm, the ringgit rose to 4.0805/0850 against the greenback from Tuesday's close of 4.0835/0880.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said market sentiment appeared to be focused on the US Consumer Price Index (CPI) data due later tonight. "The US inflation rate is expected to accelerate to 3.6 per cent in September based on consensus estimates. The reading is key as it will shape the Federal Open Market Committee's (FOMC) decision (later) this month," he told Bernama.
At the close, the ringgit traded lower against a basket of major currencies.
It climbed against the Japanese yen to 2.5751/5781 from 2.5833/5864 at Tuesday's close, inched down against the British pound to 5.4132/4192 from 5.4057/4177 and eased against the euro to 4.5673/5723 from 4.5654/5704.
Against its Asean peers, the local note gained against the Indonesian rupiah to 227.9/228.2 from 228.1/228.4 and was little changed against the Philippine peso at 6.50/6.51 from 6.49/6.50.
It edged up against the Singapore dollar to 3.1829/1267 from 3.1902/1940 at yesterday's close and gained against the Thai baht to 12.1498/1672 from 12.1663/1844.

Title: Nazir Hussin spends 2 hours at MACC over asset declaration notice
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Former Yayasan Bank Rakyat chairman Datuk Seri Nazir Hussin Akhtar Hussin spent about two hours at the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) headquarters.
Nazir was called in to receive a notice under Section 36 of the MACC Act 2009, which requires individuals to declare their assets.
He told reporters that his legal team had filed an injunction application at the Kuala Lumpur High Court yesterday to challenge the notice and prevent the MACC from enforcing it.
He said he could be arrested by the MACC despite the pending application and urged the commission to respect the legal process.
On Oct 1, the MACC remanded two corporate figures, brothers in their 40s and 50s who hold the titles Datuk Seri and Datuk Wira, for five days to assist investigations into alleged collusion and abuse of power involving an investment worth about RM10 million.
Initial investigations found that
the brothers
were suspected of colluding with an officer of an education-based foundation to approve an investment in a company owned by the elder brother in 2020.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: JAG to acquire a freehold land in Shah Alam to expand waste management business
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: JAG Bhd's unit JAG Renewable Energy Sdn Bhd has entered into a sale and purchase agreement with Kobe Steel Ltd to acquire a freehold land in Hicom Industrial Estate, Shah Alam, for RM36.89 million.
In a statement, the group said the acquisition was part of its proposed expansion of its total waste management business, which requires a total capital investment of about RM60 million, including land and equipment.
JAG said the expansion would involve establishing new production lines and increasing storage capacity to strengthen its processing capabilities and operational flexibility.
The total capital requirement of RM60 million includes the cost of the land and equipment.
The group expects the expansion to position it to capture growing resource recovery opportunities as Malaysia's digital infrastructure, renewable energy and electrification sectors expand.
JAG said investments in data centres, solar energy infrastructure and electric vehicles were expected to generate increasing volumes of recyclable materials at the end of their useful lives.
The expansion would enhance the group's ability to recover valuable materials from these waste streams through its existing recycling and resource recovery capabilities.
JAG executive director Datuk Ng Meow Giak said the acquisition is not merely an addition to the group's industrial asset base, but a strategic investment to support the next stage of its total waste management business expansion.
As Malaysia continues investing in digital infrastructure, renewable energy and electrification, new waste streams will gradually emerge as these assets reach the end of their lifecycle, he said.
"End-of-life data centre hardware, solar panels and electric vehicle (EV) batteries will require specialised recycling, material recovery and environmentally responsible waste management solutions.
"By expanding our processing capacity and storage capabilities today, we are positioning JAG to capture these future opportunities while continuing to support our customers with reliable, compliant and environmentally responsible waste management solutions," he said.
Waste management remains a highly regulated industry with significant technical, operational and compliance barriers to entry, and that building the infrastructure and recovery capabilities, as well as regulatory readiness required to support future waste streams takes time.
"This expansion allows us to prepare ahead of demand, strengthen our ability to recover higher-value materials from increasingly complex waste streams and reinforce JAG's long-term role in supporting Malaysia's circular economy," he noted.
The acquisition will be financed through a combination of internally generated funds for the 10 per cent deposit and bank borrowings for the remaining purchase consideration.
Moving ahead, the proposed acquisition is expected to strengthen JAG's long-term growth by providing additional industrial space to support future production lines, storage capacity and operational requirements.
Beyond supporting its existing industrial waste recycling activities, the expansion is expected to position the group to capture emerging end-of-life recycling opportunities arising from data centre hardware, solar panels and EV batteries as these infrastructure assets mature over time.

Title: Stroke survivor faces RM91,657 bill over Bitcoin mining
Article:
KUANTAN: A stroke survivor is facing a RM91,657 compound after her house in Cherating was allegedly used for illegal
Bitcoin mining,
leaving the property damaged.
Rabiatul Adawiyah Abdul Rahman, 35, said she had no reason to suspect wrongdoing as her monthly electricity bills ranged from RM6 to RM30 and her rent was paid promptly.
She said she agreed to rent out the house for RM850 a month after a man met her at her food stall in Balok with his wife and child, provided the required details and paid the deposit.
The tenant moved in on April 1 and later texted her that he would be working offshore while his wife stayed with her in-laws.
Rabiatul suffered a stroke on May 12, which prevented her from visiting the property.
On Sept 27, a neighbour alerted her that police and Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) workers had visited the house.
"I discovered that the premises had been used for Bitcoin mining. The walls, ceiling and toilets were damaged, with burn marks and holes everywhere. The house was left in a mess," she said.
She lodged a police report and was later informed that the MyKad details and phone number provided by the tenant belonged to other people.
Rabiatul alleged that the syndicate had tampered with the electricity supply and stolen power directly from the main pole.
She is seeking help to resolve the compound, as the electricity account is registered under her name and the tenants have disappeared.
"My husband, who works as a wireman, has stopped working to care for me. TNB wants me to pay the amount and has offered an instalment plan, but I feel this is unfair because the scammers are still free," she said.
Indera Mahkota Umno division chief Muhammad Faiz Hashim, who met Rabiatul, told the New Straits Times that nine other landlords in the area had allegedly experienced similar incidents after renting their properties to tenants who used them for illegal Bitcoin mining.
"All the victims are from low-income backgrounds. I am trying to bring them together to explore ways to assist them, including holding discussions with TNB. They are under immense pressure to pay such huge penalties," he said.
During Op Steal, a crackdown on illegal Bitcoin mining using stolen electricity in May,
property owners
were advised to transfer electricity accounts to their tenants' names when renting out their properties.

Title: Perlis power plant project requires funding commitment of up to RM479.4mil to Kinergy Advancement's unit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The maximum funding commitment for the development of the Eentier Perlis power plant to KAB Energy Holdings Sdn Bhd (KABEH), the wholly owned subsidiary of Kinergy Advancement Bhd (KAB), is RM479.4 million.
This being the 51 per cent of the total equity portion of the project of RM940 million, said KAB in a filing with Bursa Malaysia. The group is placing out 10 per cent of its shares to raise RM49.35 million to fund the equity portion.
The total project cost for the Phase 1 of the Perlis power plan stands at RM4.7 billion. External debt financing is planned to cover 80 per cent of the cost, while the remaining 20 per cent, or RM940 million, to be funded via capital injections from KABEH and B.Grimm Power.
The final equity structure will only be executed after the letter of notification (LoN) is issued by the Energy Commission (EC), said KAB in a filing with Bursa Malaysia today (Wednesday).
On Sept 25, KAB announced that it is proposing to place out up to 218.5 million new ordinary shares, representing 10 per cent of the total number of issued shares of the group, to raise RM79.75 million.
Malacca Securities Sdn Bhd is the principal adviser and placement agent for the exercise.
The company is undertaking the private placement in advance to ensure financial readiness within the six-month window following LoN issuance.
Besides the private placement proceeds of RM49.35 million, KABEH plans to fund its RM479.40 million obligation through internally generated funds and/or bank borrowings, supported by existing cash and bank balances of approximately RM155.8 million.
Development details and timeline for Eentier Perlis power plant
The proposed power plant is set to be developed on a brownfield site of a previous 650MW plant located in Simpang Empat, Perlis.
The former plant operated from 2003 until its retirement in March 2024 and has since been decommissioned, with demolition and site clearing works currently underway.
Existing infrastructure on site includes a 132/275 kilovolt (kV) switchyard, a gas metering station, and a 56 megalitres per day (MLD) water treatment plant, which may be utilised by project entity Eentier for the combined cycle gas turbine (CCGT) development.
The land is registered under Teknologi Tenaga Perlis Consortium Sdn Bhd (TTPC), which is 80 per cent owned by Jati Cakerawala Sdn Bhd, while Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) owns the rest.
KABEH holds a 51 per cent equity interest in Jati, while the remaining 49 per cent is held by B.Grimm Power.
The initial LoN (iLoN) for the project was secured on Dec 2, 2025.
Discussions are currently ongoing with the EC regarding technical and commercial terms, as well as document exchanges.
Pending the conclusion of these talks, the LoN and power purchase agreement (PPA) for Phase 1 (750 MW) remain pending, with the LoN anticipated in the fourth quarter of 2026 or the first quarter of 2027.
To ensure project readiness, consortium partner B.Grimm Power has secured the required gas turbine via a reservation agreement, which will be novated to Eentier upon issuance of the LoN.
Contingency allocations and working capital
Should KABEH ultimately not be involved in the Eentier Perlis power plant project, any pre-development expenses incurred will be non-refundable, said KAB. In such a scenario, the proceeds allocated for the power plant will be redirected toward KABEH's ongoing renewable energy (RE) projects.
These include the Gerik and Slim River mini hydropower plants in Perak, with combined project value of RM147.66 million.
KAB manages 24 projects with a total contract and/or concession value of approximately RM1.35 billion.

Title: No police reports lodged alleging Zara Qairina was murdered, court told
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: No police reports alleging that the late Zara Qairina Mahathir had been murdered, injured or struck with a blunt object were received, the Coroner's Court was told.
Investigating officer Inspector Wong Yew Zhung confirmed this when lawyer Abdul Fikry Jaafar Abdullah asked whether police had received reports concerning the alleged incidents.
Fikry:
At that time, none of Zara's family members had informed you that she had been bullied by senior students, correct?
Wong:
Correct.
Fikry:
At that time, no witnesses had come forward claiming that Zara had been bullied to the point that it caused her death, correct?
Wong:
Correct.
Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan later questioned Wong about the 200 people involved in the investigation, including 152 students residing in the hostel.
Amir:
Of the 200 individuals, or specifically the 152 students staying at the RA hostel block, was it the case that throughout your investigation, not a single person witnessed what happened to Zara before she was found on the lower level?
Wong:
Correct.
Amir:
Can you confirm again that, as stated in your witness statement, there were 152 students residing at the hostel block, but not all 152 were interviewed to assist in the investigation, correct?
Wong:
Correct.
Amir:
And following that, can you confirm that no one witnessed what happened to Zara before she was found on the ground level of the hostel?
Wong:
Correct.
Zara was found unconscious on the ground floor of her school hostel on July 16, 2025, and was pronounced dead the following day at Queen Elizabeth Hospital.
Amir has fixed Friday for submissions.

Title: No family ties between five students and VIPs or politicians, Zara inquest told
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Police found no family ties between Students A, B, C, D and E and any VIPs, VVIPs or politicians, the Coroner's Court was told.
Investigating officer Inspector Wong Yew Zhung also testified that his investigation found no evidence of protection, influence or other intervention by VIPs, VVIPs or politicians to help the students evade legal action.
The 83rd witness said this when questioned by lawyer Abdul Fikry Jaafar Abdullah during the inquest into the death of Zara Qairina Mahathir.
Fikry: Based on your investigation, did you find that any VIPs, VVIPs or politicians had family ties with Students A, B, C, D and E?
Wong: No.
Fikry: Based on your investigation, did you find any evidence that any VIPs, VVIPs or politicians had provided protection, exerted influence or taken any action to help Students A, B, C, D and E evade legal action in this case?
Wong: None.
Meanwhile, Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan asked Wong to explain his understanding of the terms VIP and VVIP referred to in the lawyer's questions.
Wong said he understood a VIP to include someone such as a social media influencer, but maintained that no influencer had pressured him or approached other witnesses in connection with the five students.
Asked whether he had faced any pressure from any party throughout the investigation, Wong said the stress he experienced came from handling the case itself and that he had tried his best to remain professional.
Zara was found unconscious on the ground floor of her school hostel on July 16, 2025, and was pronounced dead the following day at Queen Elizabeth Hospital (QEH).
Her remains were exhumed on Aug 9, 2025, before a post-mortem examination was conducted the following day at the Forensic Medicine Department of QEH.
On Aug 20, 2025, five minors, identified by the pseudonyms Students A, B, C, D and E, were charged in the Court for Children with insulting Zara. All five pleaded not guilty.
The inquest began on Sept 3, 2025, to establish the cause and circumstances of Zara's death, including whether any criminal elements were involved.

Title: [UPDATED] Nazir Hussin refuses MACC asset declaration notice
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  Former Yayasan Bank Rakyat chairman Datuk Seri Nazir Hussin Akhtar Hussin has refused to accept an asset declaration notice issued by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).
The notice was issued as part of an investigation into suspected misappropriation and abuse of position involving investments worth about RM10 million.
Nazir, his wife and an assistant
were summoned
to MACC headquarters in Putrajaya today to assist in the investigation.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said Nazir was called in to receive a notice requiring him to declare his assets under Section 36 of the MACC Act 2009.
Nazir refused to accept the notice, citing an injunction application he filed at the Kuala Lumpur High Court yesterday to prevent enforcement of the directive.
"His wife and assistant had their statements recorded for about an hour and 30 minutes.
"Nazir, his wife and assistant arrived at MACC headquarters at about 11am today, while his wife and assistant were allowed to leave at 1.15pm," he said.
Abd Halim said the questioning and attempted service of the asset declaration notice took place at MACC headquarters this morning.
The investigation centres on suspected misappropriation and abuse of position involving investment dealings worth about RM10 million.
Nazir arrived at MACC headquarters with two lawyers at about 11am and was still there as of 1pm.
He told reporters that he had filed an injunction application at the Kuala Lumpur High Court yesterday to prevent enforcement of the notice.
He also claimed he could be arrested by the MACC and urged the commission to respect the legal process and await the court's decision on his application.

Title: RTD Ops Luxury: The price of looking rich
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Cheah, 36, bought a second-hand BMW X6 for RM40,000, hoping the luxury badge would help him project success and win people's trust.
But the cost of keeping the car on the road proved harder to manage than the bargain he had struck.
"People look at what you wear and what you drive before deciding whether they can trust you. Some think you are not doing well if you do not drive a luxury car," he said.
The sales executive bought the first-generation BMW X6 from a friend who runs a used-car dealership.
He admitted that he and some of his peers had underestimated the cost of ownership, particularly insurance and road tax.
"The appeal of a luxury vehicle goes beyond the drive itself. It is also about how others perceive me," he said.
Cheah said the Transport Ministry's decision to allow private vehicle owners to use digital road tax instead of displaying a physical disc had made things easier, particularly during enforcement operations.
"Many people assume that if you can afford a luxury car, you should have no problem paying for its insurance and road tax," he said.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke
announced the change
in February 2023, removing the requirement for private vehicle owners to display physical road tax discs.
Cheah admitted motorists had to take responsibility for complying with the law, especially amid concerns about dangerous driving and road accidents.
"Lifestyle is equally important," he said, describing the pressure to maintain an image of success despite the financial burden.
Meanwhile, Tow-truck operator S. Siva, 46, who has spent more than 20 years in the business, said some luxury-car owners were among the most difficult customers when their vehicles had to be towed.
"They have all sorts of excuses when it their cars towed," he said, adding that some owners allowed their road tax and insurance to lapse because of the cost.
"In my experience, luxury-car owners are more likely to let their road tax lapse. You rarely see locally made cars on the road without valid road tax," he added.
Yesterday, the Johor Road Transport Department (RTD)
seized four luxury vehicles
during Ops Luxury after inspections found that their road tax had expired and they had no valid insurance.
The vehicles were a BMW X6, a Mercedes-Benz CLA 45, a Mercedes-Benz GLE-Class and a Toyota Alphard. Their combined value was estimated at nearly RM1 million.
Ops Luxury targets luxury vehicles whose owners flout road transport laws, including failing to renew road tax or maintain valid insurance, as well as offences involving driving licences and vehicle technical requirements.
Johor RTD director Zulkarnain Yasin said enforcement would continue to ensure vehicles on public roads complied with the law and met safety requirements.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Russia detains Japanese journalist on suspicion of spying
Article:
MOSCOW: Russia said on Tuesday it had detained a Japanese journalist on suspicion of espionage and accused Tokyo of using media correspondents to gather intelligence, marking a new low in bilateral relations that have worsened sharply in recent months.
Russia's Foreign Ministry identified the journalist as Yuki Imai and the FSB security agency said he worked for the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper, which is a regional newspaper for Japan's northern island.
He was detained in the far eastern Sakhalin region the day before he planned to leave the country, the FSB said without specifying the date. It accused him of collecting and storing information on Russia's defence capabilities for intelligence purposes that it said could be used against Russian security.
The Hokkaido Shimbun did not confirm the journalist's identity, saying only that it was still confirming details and that the reporter's safety was its top priority.
Japanese Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said on Wednesday that Tokyo had asked Russian authorities for information and called for fair treatment and humanitarian consideration for the national.
A senior official of the Japanese Foreign Ministry later summoned the Russian ambassador to Japan and lodged a protest for detaining the Japanese national and unilaterally issuing statements regarding the matter without providing explanation to Tokyo, the ministry said in a statement.
The director-general of the Foreign Ministry's European Affairs Bureau, Kimitake Nakamura, also asked the ambassador, Nikolay Nozdrev, to set up an opportunity swiftly to meet the detained journalist, the ministry said.
In a Russian state TV video report, three masked men in black uniforms handcuffed a man lying on the ground as a voice off camera said he was suspected of spying.
The video showed the man being accompanied by two FSB servicemen onto a plane, then in a cage in a Moscow court, which ordered him detained for nearly two months.
It is the most high-profile detainment of a foreign journalist since the 2023 detention of Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich.
Gershkovich, who says his arrest was a carefully planned FSB sting, was found guilty of espionage by a Russian court, sentenced to 16 years and then freed in an East-West prisoner swap in August 2024.
[[nid:1555501]]
The case adds to long-running tensions between Russia and Japan, which have yet to sign a formal World War Two peace treaty due to a territorial dispute over the Kuril Islands, known in Japan as the Northern Territories.
Those tensions heightened when Japan joined Western sanctions against Moscow over the war in Ukraine, with Russia regarding Japan as an "unfriendly" country. But business ties remain with Japan a purchaser of Russian liquefied natural gas.
Then in August, Russian President Vladimir Putin visited one of the disputed islands, causing an uproar in Japan. On Tuesday, a delegation from a Chinese province visited the same island, in what appeared to signal closer coordination between Moscow and Beijing in their criticism of Tokyo.
Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova said on Tuesday that Japan had refused to consider Moscow's concerns about what she called Tokyo's "remilitarisation."
She criticised Japan's alleged use of accredited journalists in Russia to gather information that could undermine Russian security.
"We have to note that what has occurred will become an additional factor clouding the atmosphere of Russian-Japanese relations," Zakharova said.
Asked whether improving relations between Russia and the US and Japan's purchases of LNG from Russia made it difficult for Tokyo to take countermeasures, Japan's Kihara said:
"It is true that there are many issues between Japan and Russia.
"From Japan's perspective, despite the difficult situation in Japan-Russia relations, Japan has taken resolute measures based on its position. At the same time, Russia is a neighbouring country to Japan, and communication is necessary to resolve these issues."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: Education Ministry coordinating school operating procedures under new action plan
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) has begun coordinating school operating procedures based on the National Haze Action Plan (PTJK) to ensure that decisions on school closures are made in a more systematic manner, taking into account Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and health advice.
Its minister, Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, said that under the coordinated procedures, outdoor activities would be postponed when the API reading exceeds 100, while schools would be closed when the reading exceeds 200, in accordance with the PTJK.
“We need to understand that API readings can change within a short period.
“Closing schools several days in advance without taking these changes into account could result in children losing learning time even after air quality has returned to normal,” she said in a Facebook post today.
She said the ministry welcomed the National Disaster Management Agency’s (NADMA) emphasis that haze management must be guided by the PTJK, following discussions with relevant agencies.
At the same time, Fadhlina said she understood the concerns of parents who have to wait for daily decisions on school operations while the country faces haze, particularly those whose children have health problems or are more sensitive to air pollution.
As such, she said parents could keep their children at home if they were concerned about their health and safety during the haze, provided they notify the school authorities.
“The safety and health of our children remain our top priority. However, every school day also matters for their development and learning.
“I hope this coordination will provide greater certainty for parents, reduce the difficulties they face and ensure that every decision on school operations takes into account both the health of children and the continuity of their education in a balanced manner,” she added. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar extends donation to Makkal Osai senior editor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 (Bernama) — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended a donation to
Makkal Osai
